status_as_of_cutoff: Existing facility with locally approved and contested expansion activity. Lowell Planning Board approved the 2024 site-plan alteration for nine additional modular chiller plants, four additional generators, a water-treatment building, and utility/electric infrastructure, with conditions. Lowell City Council adopted an amended data-center moratorium on March 10, 2026 by 10 yeas / 1 abstain. MassDEP affirmed Air Quality Plan Approval NE-25-002 for eight emergency generators on March 27, 2026 and denied reconsideration on July 10, 2026. Lowell's current Planning Board page lists 2 Prince Ave / 1 Markley Way for a definitive subdivision hearing on August 17, 2026. No CO, energization, partial-live, full-buildout, or MW capacity evidence was located.
evidence_grade: A for official local/MassDEP permit and moratorium actions; C for physical construction/energization because no current CO, utility energization, or in-service record was located.

actions.government_body: Lowell Planning Board / Development Services application package
actions.result_status: Stantec submitted a site-plan review package for Markley Group's continued redevelopment of 1 Markley Way / former 2 Prince Avenue, including nine additional modular chiller plants, four additional generators, a water-treatment building, utility repairs, retaining walls, and electric infrastructure.

actions.access_caveat: Application transmittal; not itself an approval.
actions.evidence_note: Official Lowell project file documents proposed scope but does not establish MW capacity.

actions.result_status: Planning Board minutes state Markley Group sought approval to alter the industrial site with nine chillers, four generators, a water-treatment building, and related improvements; the Board approved the item with conditions by unanimous 5-0 vote.
actions.case_or_ordinance_permit_number: 2 Prince Avenue, 1 Markley Way 01852 - Site Plan Review
actions.access_caveat: Approval is a local site-plan action; MassDEP air permitting and later moratorium/litigation are separate records.
actions.evidence_note: The cited minutes include conditions for MassDEP reports, drift eliminators, fire access during construction, and continuing MassDEP compliance.

actions.result_status: Council referred a motion seeking a temporary moratorium on new or expanded data centers to the City Manager/Law Department; the referral motion was adopted by an 11–0 roll call.
actions.access_caveat: The cited official minutes are dated January 13 within a January 20 packet; referral is not final ordinance adoption.
actions.evidence_note: Official action; no Markley construction or permit disposition inferred.

actions.action_type: first reading of proposed zoning ordinance
actions.result_status: The official packet describes a proposed ordinance adding a 360-day moratorium on data centers and says it would be referred to the Planning Board for public hearing and recommendation before any final Council vote.
actions.vote_tally: first reading; final adoption tally not stated
actions.access_caveat: First reading and draft ordinance, not final adoption.
actions.evidence_note: Official zoning process; moratorium status is not conflated with a project permit denial.

actions.result_status: Official City Council minutes state the Council held the second reading/hearing and adopted the amended data-center moratorium; Planning Board recommendations on changes to the moratorium were also adopted.
actions.vote_tally: 10 yes / 0 no / 1 abstain on adoption; 10 yes / 0 no / 1 abstain on Planning Board recommendations
actions.access_caveat: Official minutes establish Council adoption and vote tally; the precise codified effective-date text was not separately located.
actions.evidence_note: Government regulatory record, not project approval.

actions.result_status: MassDEP's Commissioner adopted the Recommended Final Decision, granted summary decision to MassDEP and Markley Group, LLC, and affirmed Air Quality Plan Approval NE-25-002 for the Lowell facility.
actions.case_or_ordinance_permit_number: OADR Docket No. 2025-022; DEP File No. 24-AQ02F-0001-APP; Approval No. NE-25-002
actions.access_caveat: Final agency decision affirms the air permit; it does not document construction completion, energization, or MW capacity.
actions.evidence_note: State permitting appeal record for eight emergency generators.

actions.result_status: The Board's minutes state that a moratorium on data centers applied generally, not only to Markley, while reviewing a preliminary subdivision at 2 Prince Avenue/1 Markley Way; the subdivision vote itself was unanimous 5–0 and was not a data-center approval.
actions.case_or_ordinance_permit_number: 2 Prince Avenue / 1 Markley Way preliminary subdivision
actions.access_caveat: Minutes distinguish the subdivision application from the proposed use; no data-center permit was decided in the cited item.
actions.evidence_note: Official planning record preserves the distinction between property activity and data-center approval.

actions.result_status: The Board approved The Dude's Place, LLC preliminary subdivision for 2 Prince Avenue / 1 Markley Way by unanimous 5-0 vote; minutes state the subdivision covered 2 Prince Avenue, 56 Newhall Street, and 48 Newhall Street, creating four parcels and a proposed private subdivision roadway, and that preliminary subdivision approval did not authorize construction or a data-center expansion.
actions.case_or_ordinance_permit_number: 2 Prince Avenue (1 Markley Way) preliminary subdivision
actions.access_caveat: Subdivision applicant differs from Markley Group; the minutes frame this as property/subdivision process, not a site-plan or data-center use approval.
actions.evidence_note: Official planning minutes document related parcel activity and community concerns without proving buildout.

actions.result_status: MassDEP denied the Lowell residents' motion for reconsideration of the March 27 Final Decision and left the affirmed Air Quality Plan Approval in place.
